findings_to_judge.finding: FY27 guidance requires a four-point inflection in the revenue trend starting in the quarter being reported: FY26 total revenue was $512.7m less $108.9m of Global Knowledge equals ~$403.8m of continuing (TDS) revenue, so the $388-406m FY27 guide brackets flat; Q1 FY27 was $94.5m, -4.7% YoY, which leaves the guide midpoint needing Q2-Q4 at about -0.7% versus a Q1 running at -4.7% and a company that itself flagged 'softness in government bookings' and consumer down 21%.

Q2 FY27 (May 1 - Jul 31, 2026) is new CFO Ron Kisling's first full quarter — he started 2026-05-20, twenty days before the June 9 reaffirmation — and his predecessor John Frederick's transition-advisory contract expired 2026-09-04, five days before this print, so the first quarter he can fully own is the first one reported without the author of the inherited guidance still under contract.

The two enterprise-learning comps that reported after Skillsoft last spoke on June 9 disagree with each other, and the closer pure-play comp is the positive one: Docebo (2026-08-07) reported ARR +9.5% YoY, a second consecutive quarter of re-acceleration, and RAISED full-year revenue guidance by $3.5m citing enterprise strength, while Coursera (2026-07-29) reported enterprise NRR down to 91% on L&D budget pressure.

Tonight is the first call at which a refinancing update is contractually due: on 2026-06-09 Hovsepian said addressing the debt maturities becomes 'management's top financial priority' once the Global Knowledge sale closes, and it closed 2026-07-06 — a $574.6m term loan due 2028-07-16 against $115.6m cash and a ~$60m equity, so any constructive statement is worth far more in percentage terms than silence costs.
